reviewedBy: Claude Opus 5 — gave photos a real share card; they were unfurling at 150x224
method: Measured the actual variant and rendered the actual cards, not read from code. Before: the photo page set og:image to the raw Cloudflare 'thumbnail' variant. Fetched it: 150x224 pixels, 10 KB. Facebook's own documentation states 'The minimum allowed image dimension is 200 x 200 pixels' and recommends 1200x630 at 1.91:1, so a shared photo unfurled with no image or a postage stamp on a page whose entire subject is a photograph — while albums had had a proper generated 1200x630 card since the earlier share-card work. The code comment claiming the thumbnail was 'still high quality' was simply wrong about its size. After: /photo/[id]/og.png renders a 1200x630 card via the existing og-card module, verified by rendering it — 1200x630 PNG returned for DSC06067, DSC05553 and TRoiyO-DSC05553. Chose a split layout over the album card's full-bleed cover because 16,140 of 19,767 photos are portrait (82%): cover-cropping a 2:3 action shot to 1.91:1 keeps a band through the torso and loses arms and ball. Confirmed visually in both orientations — a portrait frame sits whole in the left panel, and a 1.5 landscape frame letterboxes in the same panel without cropping. The card route resolves through resolvePhotoByImageKey rather than its own query, so the 113 colliding keys get the right photo's card: DSC05553 and TRoiyO-DSC05553 render two different images (sha256 differs). /photo/null/og.png returns 404 without a database round trip. og:image:width and og:image:height are now emitted (1200x630) and are truthful because we render the card ourselves.
